docs.title: labctl
docs.text:
Local dev labs without the nonsense.

labctl creates small, connected, machine-like development environments using containers. No Docker Compose files, no networking config, no YAML sprawl. One command per machine.

docs.title: The idea
docs.text: You want a Linux box with Node installed. Or a Postgres database your API can talk to by name. Or three machines on the same network so you can test a microservice setup. labctl makes that a few commands instead of a side-quest into container orchestration.

docs.title: What it looks like
docs.text:
# Create two machines on the same network
labctl create api --template node
labctl create db  --template postgres

# They can already resolve each other by name
labctl shell api
curl http://db:5432  # just works

# See everything running
labctl list

# Done for the day
labctl destroy api
labctl destroy db

docs.title: Core principles
docs.text:
• Machines, not containers. You think in terms of dev machines, not Docker implementation details.
  • Connected by default. Every machine lands on a shared network with DNS. Bare hostnames work out of the box.
  • Zero config for common cases. Templates handle the Dockerfile, ports, and volumes. You just pick a name and go.
  • Docker labels as state. No local state files, no database. Docker itself is the source of truth.

docs.title: Current status
docs.text: labctl is in active development. MVP-0 (create, list, shell, destroy) is complete and working. Templates, lifecycle commands, and VS Code integration are next.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text: Head to the Quickstart to install labctl and create your first machine in under two minutes.

docs.title: Cheat Sheet
docs.text: Copy-pasteable recipes for common labctl workflows.

docs.title: Create and jump in
docs.text:
labctl create dev
labctl shell dev

docs.title: See what's running
docs.text: labctl list

docs.title: Tear it down
docs.text: labctl destroy dev

docs.title: API + database
docs.text:
Create two machines. They resolve each other by name automatically.

labctl create api
labctl create db --template postgres

Verify connectivity from the API machine:

labctl shell api
ping db          # resolves via Docker DNS
curl db:5432     # reaches Postgres
exit

Clean up both:

labctl destroy api
labctl destroy db --volumes

docs.title: Three-tier setup
docs.text:
labctl create frontend --template node
labctl create backend  --template python
labctl create db       --template postgres

From any machine, the other two are reachable by name:

labctl shell backend
curl http://frontend:3000   # Node dev server
psql -h db -U postgres      # Postgres
exit

docs.title: Template shortcuts
docs.text:
What you want Command Blank Ubuntu box labctl create dev Node.js labctl create api --template node Python labctl create api --template python Go labctl create api --template go Postgres labctl create db --template postgres Redis labctl create cache --template redis

Templates coming soon

The full template set (node, python, go, postgres, redis) ships in Phase 5. Currently only the blank template is available.

docs.title: Volumes and data persistence
docs.text:
Postgres and Redis templates create named volumes so data survives container restarts.

# Destroy machine but keep data
labctl destroy db

# Destroy machine AND its data
labctl destroy db --volumes

docs.title: Quick reference
docs.text: Task Command Install labctl pipx install git+https://github.com/maccalsa/labctl.git Create a machine labctl create NAME [-t TEMPLATE] List machines labctl list Open a shell labctl shell NAME Destroy a machine labctl destroy NAME [--volumes] Check version labctl --version Get help labctl --help or labctl COMMAND --help

docs.title: CLI Reference

docs.text:
Option Short Description --version -V Show version and exit --help Show help and exit 
labctl --version

docs.title: labctl create
docs.text: Create a new dev machine from a template.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: labctl create NAME [--template TEMPLATE]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Required Description NAME Yes Name for the machine. Used as the container hostname and DNS name on the network.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Short Default Description --template -t blank Template to use for the machine.

docs.title: What happens
docs.text:
1. The template image is built (or reused if cached).
  2. A container named labctl-NAME is created with management labels.
  3. The container is attached to the labctl-net network with NAME as its DNS hostname.
  4. The container starts.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Create a machine with the default (blank) template
labctl create my-dev

# Create a machine with a specific template
labctl create api --template node
labctl create db -t postgres

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Machine created successfully 1 Error (duplicate name, unknown template, Docker unavailable)

docs.title: labctl list
docs.text: Show all labctl-managed machines.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: labctl list

docs.title: Output columns
docs.text: Column Description Name Machine name (without the labctl- prefix) Template Template the machine was created from Status running or exited Ports Mapped ports in container_port->host_port format

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# List all machines
labctl list

# Example output:
#   Machines
# ┏━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓
# ┃ Name ┃ Template ┃ Status  ┃ Ports       ┃
# ┡━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━┩
# │ api  │ node     │ running │ 3000→32768  │
# │ db   │ postgres │ running │ 5432→32769  │
# └──────┴──────────┴─────────┴─────────────┘

When no machines exist, prints "No machines found."

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success (even if no machines exist) 1 Error (Docker unavailable)

docs.title: labctl destroy
docs.text: Remove a dev machine.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: labctl destroy NAME [--volumes] [--force]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Required Description NAME Yes Machine to destroy.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Short Default Description --volumes false Also delete named volumes associated with the machine. --force -f false Skip confirmation.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Removes the container for the named machine.
  • If the machine has named volumes (e.g. from a postgres template), labctl warns you and lists the volume names. Use --volumes to delete them too.
  • If the machine doesn't exist, exits with a clear error.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Destroy a machine (volumes are preserved)
labctl destroy api

# Destroy a machine and its volumes
labctl destroy db --volumes

# Destroy without confirmation
labctl destroy api --force

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Machine destroyed 1 Error (machine not found, Docker unavailable)

docs.title: labctl shell
docs.text: Open an interactive shell inside a running machine.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: labctl shell NAME

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Required Description NAME Yes Machine to open a shell in.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Detects the best available shell: prefers /bin/bash, falls back to /bin/sh.
  • Attaches an interactive session with a TTY.
  • Propagates the shell's exit code.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Open a shell
labctl shell my-dev

# Run a quick command (via the shell)
labctl shell my-dev
> echo "hello from inside"
> exit

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 Shell session exited cleanly 1 Error (machine not found, machine not running) other Propagated from the shell process

Machine must be running

If the machine is stopped, labctl tells you to start it first: labctl start NAME (available in a future release).

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: Get labctl installed and create your first dev machine in under two minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.11+ — check with python3 --version
  • Docker — running and accessible (docker info should work)
  • pipx (recommended) — install with pip install --user pipx

docs.title: Recommended: pipx (isolated, one command)
docs.text:
pipx install git+https://github.com/maccalsa/labctl.git

This installs labctl into its own virtualenv and puts it on your $PATH. No conflicts with other Python packages.

docs.title: Alternative: pip
docs.text: pip install git+https://github.com/maccalsa/labctl.git

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
labctl --version
# labctl 0.1.0

docs.title: 1. Create a machine
docs.text:
labctl create my-dev

This pulls the blank template (Ubuntu 24.04 with bash, curl, and git), builds the image, and starts a container named labctl-my-dev on the shared labctl-net network.

docs.title: 2. See it running
docs.text:
labctl list

You'll see a table with your machine's name, template, status, and any mapped ports.

docs.title: 3. Jump in
docs.text:
labctl shell my-dev

You're now inside the machine with a bash shell. Poke around, install things, run code. When you're done, exit to return.

docs.title: 4. Clean up
docs.text:
labctl destroy my-dev

The container is removed. If the machine had named volumes, labctl tells you they still exist and how to remove them.

docs.title: Two machines that talk to each other
docs.text:
Every labctl machine lands on the same Docker network (labctl-net) with DNS resolution by name.

labctl create api
labctl create backend

# From inside 'api', you can reach 'backend' by hostname
labctl shell api
ping backend    # resolves immediately
exit

# Tear them both down
labctl destroy api
labctl destroy backend
